record.original_question: For a rational polygon P, the quadratic constants c_*(P) and c^*(P) are defined by inequalities c_*(P) l^2 <= f_P(l) <= c^*(P) l^2 for all sufficiently large l. Find efficient estimates for these quadratic constants.

evidence.quote: There exist numbers 0 < c_*(P) <= c^*(P) < infinity such that c_*(P) l^2 <= f_P(l) <= c^*(P) l^2 for sufficiently large l. We will refer to these inequalities as the quadratic bounds on periodic billiard orbits. The numbers c_*(P), c^*(P) are the quadratic constants.
Problem 12. Find efficient estimates for quadratic constants.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a rational polygon, that is, a polygon in the Euclidean plane all of whose interior angles are rational multiples of π. A billiard trajectory in P is the path of a point mass moving in straight lines inside P and reflecting from the boundary according to the law of equal angles (with trajectories hitting a vertex left undefined). A periodic billiard trajectory is one that closes up after finitely many reflections; periodic trajectories occur in parallel families ("strips") of equal length, and one defines

  f_P(ℓ) = number of strips of periodic billiard trajectories in P of length at most ℓ.

It is known that there exist constants 0 < c_*(P) ≤ c^*(P) < ∞ such that

  c_*(P) ℓ^2  ≤  f_P(ℓ)  ≤  c^*(P) ℓ^2

for all sufficiently large ℓ. The numbers c_*(P) and c^*(P) are called the quadratic constants of P.

Problem: Provide efficient (computable, sharp, or otherwise quantitatively useful) estimates for the quadratic constants c_*(P) and c^*(P) of a rational polygon P. In particular, give methods that, for as wide a class of rational polygons as possible, produce explicit upper and lower bounds on c_*(P) and c^*(P), and ideally identify the limit c(P) = lim_{ℓ→∞} f_P(ℓ)/ℓ^2 when it exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The quadratic bounds on the counting function f_P(ℓ) for periodic billiard orbits in rational polygons are due to Masur (existence of quadratic upper and lower bounds). Exact asymptotics (Siegel–Veech-type constants) are known only for special families (e.g., Veech polygons such as the regular n-gons and lattice surfaces), where c_*(P) = c^*(P) = c(P) can be computed via Eskin–Masur–Zorich theory. For a general rational polygon, no efficient or sharp estimates of c_*(P), c^*(P) are known, and the problem of computing or bounding them effectively is widely regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Rational billiards and flat structures (Masur–Tabachnikov)
status_evidence.snippet: Quadratic upper and lower bounds on the number of periodic strips in rational polygons; exact asymptotics known for Veech surfaces via Siegel–Veech constants.
status_evidence.claim: Effective estimates of the quadratic constants for general rational polygons are not available; only special (Veech) cases admit explicit computation.

status_evidence.title: Survey Lecture on Billiards (R. Schwartz)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses growth of periodic orbits in polygonal billiards and the lack of effective constants outside the lattice/Veech setting.
status_evidence.claim: Estimating the quadratic constants for general rational polygons remains an open problem.
